name: Center Ride Out
date_note: Friday, April 23 through Sunday, April 25, 2027. Check-in is Thursday, April 22, 3:00 to 7:00 pm, at the Los Angeles LGBT Center. The first ride was April 24–26, 2026.
founded_by: the Los Angeles LGBT Center, as an AIDS/LifeCycle legacy event
registration_note: Registration is $95 for 3-day riders and $195 for 1-day riders. The fundraising minimum is $2,500 for 3-day riders (the ride's page gives April 2, 2027) and $250 for 1-day riders (by April 23). A Community Fund can cover a minimum or a registration; its 2027 applications open in February.

distances.label: 3 days, 200+ miles
distances.note: Los Angeles to Ojai on Day 1, 80-plus miles. A day in camp or an out-and-back on Day 2. Ojai back to the coast near Santa Monica on Day 3, 80-plus miles.

distances.label: 1 day
distances.note: 1-day riders ride Day 2 only, Saturday, April 24.

terrain: Canyon and mountain roads north out of Los Angeles to Ojai, then backcountry roads and the coast on the way back
participants: More than 300 riders and volunteers on the first ride in 2026
cost: $95 registration for 3-day riders, $195 for 1-day riders, plus the fundraising minimum. A Basecamp pass for people who aren't riding or volunteering is $50.
summary: Center Ride Out is a three-day, 200-plus-mile supported ride that raises money for the Los Angeles LGBT Center. In 2027 it runs April 23–25: Los Angeles to Ojai, a day at camp by a lake, then back along the coast to a finish near Santa Monica. Registration is $95 and the fundraising minimum is $2,500 for 3-day riders. The first ride, in 2026, went from Los Angeles to San Diego and raised $830,511.
history: AIDS/LifeCycle ran from San Francisco to Los Angeles for seven days every June and raised more than $300 million for HIV and AIDS services from 1994 on. Its last ride was in 2025. The Los Angeles LGBT Center announced Center Ride Out in November 2025 as the ride that carries that legacy in Southern California.
The first Center Ride Out was April 24–26, 2026, from Los Angeles to San Diego. The Center says it raised $830,511. For 2027 the route changes: north to Ojai, a camp there, and back down the coast.
what_to_expect: Check-in is the afternoon before, at the Center: wristbands, bike drop-off, and you meet the volunteers. Friday rolls at 6:30 am. Routes close between 3:00 and 6:00 pm, depending on the day's length.

The ride is fully supported. Rest stops come every 15 to 20 miles, lunch is on the route, and there are support vehicles, bike mechanics, a marked course and medical staff on the road and in camp. You don't have to ride every mile. A support vehicle will take you to the next stop, to lunch or to camp.

Camp is in Ojai, by a lake. The Center calls it Queer Summer Camp: swimming, canoeing, a DJ, s'mores, massages and a stage program at night. Saturday you can stay there or ride an out-and-back. Sunday rolls by 7:00 am and ends at a finish line festival by the ocean with food and music.

faq.q: When is Center Ride Out in 2027?
faq.a: April 23–25, 2027, a Friday through a Sunday. Check-in is Thursday, April 22, from 3:00 to 7:00 pm at the Los Angeles LGBT Center.

faq.q: What is the Center Ride Out route?
faq.a: In 2027 it goes from Los Angeles north through canyon and mountain roads to Ojai on Day 1, 80-plus miles. Day 2 is a day in camp or an out-and-back ride. Day 3 goes from Ojai back to the coast and finishes near Santa Monica, 80-plus miles. The Center says route links come closer to the ride and the routes may change. The 2026 ride went from Los Angeles to San Diego.
$2,500 for 3-day riders and $250 for 1-day riders. Registration is $95 for three days and $195 for one.
In camp in Ojai, by a lake, on Friday and Saturday nights. The Center has not published the camp's location. People who aren't riding or volunteering can buy a $50 Basecamp pass.

faq.q: Can I ride just one day?
faq.a: Yes. 1-day riders ride Day 2, Saturday, April 24.
To the Los Angeles LGBT Center's general fund. The Center says about 89 cents of every dollar raised goes to its programs and services.
